subject: Post-call: evaluation cadence, success rubric & kickoff plan
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Patel <maya@orchidhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-15T22:12:00Z
Subject: Post-call: evaluation cadence, success rubric & kickoff plan

Hi Maya — thanks again for a productive discovery call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before scheduling the kickoff:

Summary (short)
- Goal: Validate Redwood inference for Orchid’s clinical-document classification + entity extraction flows at scale; measure latency, throughput, and precision/recall improvements against current baseline.
- Scope for this trial: ~50k documents (de-identified), two pipelines (classification + NER), readout at end of 4 weeks.

Success criteria (suggested)
- Latency: 95th percentile < 350ms on our staging configuration for typical doc size (1–3 KB).
- Throughput: sustain >= 25 req/s with <10% error rate during synthetic peak.
- Quality: classification F1 >= baseline + 10%; NER micro-F1 >= baseline + 12%.
- Stability: no more than one incident requiring mitigation during trial window.

High-level evaluation plan & timeline
- Pre-kickoff (by Aug 20): Orchid to share 500-sample de-identified dataset + test account details; Redwood security questionnaire & SOC2 evidence provided.
- Kickoff (week of Aug 22): 60-minute technical kickoff (owners, environments, data access, success rubric walkthrough).
- Execution (Aug 23–Sep 17): implementation + two weekly artifacts: (1) short runbook + (2) automated test run results. Weekly 30-minute check-ins (Mon 30m).
- Final readout (week of Sep 20): demo, metrics dashboard, decision/go-forward recommendation.

Owners
- Redwood: Stephanie (pilot lead, commercial owner), Ben (SE, technical lead), Camila (CS, onboarding & ops).
- Orchid: Maya (product lead), Devon (data lead), Legal contact for procurement.

Immediate asks for Orchid (action items)
1) Confirm kickoff week availability (Aug 22–26) and preferred timezone.
2) Share a 500-sample de-identified dataset by Aug 20 and a contact for creating a test service account.
3) Identify any additional security/compliance docs needed beyond the SOC2 pack.

Attachments included for reference: evaluation_template.xlsx (success-rubric + data sample template), redwood_poc_playbook.pdf (runbook + recommended agenda).

If this all looks good I’ll send a calendar invite for the kickoff and Ben will follow up with the technical checklist.

Thanks — look forward to getting started.

— Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

Subject: RE: Post-call: evaluation cadence, success rubric & kickoff plan — technical checklist

Thanks, Maya — putting together the technical checklist below so Orchid can start prepping infra in parallel. I’ll also attach a short SE checklist with more detail.

Required access / network
- Test service account: we need an API key tied to a staging project. Please share the contact that can create it (or we can generate and you can rotate).
- IP allowlist: staging endpoint IPs are 34.122.45.19 and 34.122.45.21 (please confirm with your infra).
- If Orchid needs VPC peering for Private deployments we can scope that after the trial.

Data & samples
- 500 de-identified docs (CSV or JSONL) with a small metadata column (document_id, source, created_at).
- For NER evaluation include gold-label span offsets in a separate file or a CoNLL-style export.

Recommended trial config (to balance cost vs performance)
- Model variant: rdxf-3b-mix-quant (recommended for NER + classification)
- Batch target: 8–16 per request for throughput; Redwood auto-batching will adapt during runs.
- KV cache: reuse across related conversations to keep warm-up low.

Kickoff agenda (30–60m)
- Introductions & roles (5m)
- Trial scope & success criteria review (10m)
- Data & access walkthrough (10m)
- Test runs & observability plan (10m)
- Next steps & calendar (5m)

Attachments: se_checklist.md (stub) — includes the exact curl examples, sample payloads, and expected responses. I’ll post the checklist to the shared Drive folder after this note.

If the IPs or model suggestion are blockers, flag them here and we’ll adjust.

— Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
